transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I'm here because... well, people have been saying they can't follow what I'm trying to explain. At work, mostly. I write artist statements and notes for clients, and they say I jump around too much. Like, I'll be talking about the texture of a piece, and then the budget, and then... I don't know, other meanings behind it. They say it doesn't make sense. So, I guess that's why I'm here.
Do you find yourself talking more quickly than usual or feeling like your thoughts are racing from one idea to the next?

Um... yeah, I guess they do. They just move fast sometimes. Like... images, and titles, or the grant language I'm supposed to be writing... colors, conversations. It's like they all just sort of... stack on top of each other. Before I can even finish one idea.
Do you often feel like you can't stop talking, or that you're speaking before you've had time to fully think?
Um... no, not really. I don't think I talk too much. I just... I just say what's there. I don't feel like I can't stop or anything.
Have you noticed that when you're trying to get your ideas across, you're speaking so quickly that others have trouble keeping up or interrupt to ask you to slow down?

Um... no, not really. I haven't noticed that. People don't usually ask me to slow down or anything. They just... they just say they don't follow the ideas. I don't think it's about how fast I'm talking.
Do you ever feel that your own thoughts are disorganized or hard to follow, even when you're not trying to explain them to someone else?

I guess... maybe sometimes. It's more that... well, it's why I came in, really. The things I write down, like my artist statements or... or notes for clients. Even when I'm just talking in meetings. It all just kind of... jumps around. From, you know, textures to budgets... to these secret meanings I see in things. And people just... they keep saying they can't follow what I'm trying to explain. So... yeah, I guess they are hard to follow.
Have you ever experienced seeing, hearing, or sensing things that others don't seem to notice, or have you ever believed something strongly that others around you don't seem to share or understand?

Um... I don't know about believing things others don't. But... sometimes, when I'm alone in my studio... I hear things. Just... a woman's voice. She's usually quiet, like she's standing behind the storage shelves, just... making comments. And sometimes I smell things, too. Like... hot metal, right next to a piece I'm working on. It's... it feels real. I always stop and check, but... there's never anyone there. Nothing is burning. It's just... me.

Do these experiences—like hearing the woman’s voice or smelling something that isn’t there—happen only when you're feeling particularly down, stressed, or excited, or do they occur even when your mood is normal?

I don't know... I guess they happen other times, too. Like, there was a month a little while ago where things were... quieter. I was sleeping okay, not feeling so... intense or unstoppable. Just kind of normal, I think. But I still heard her. The comments from behind the shelves. And I was still seeing those... hidden warnings in the materials I use. That lasted for a few weeks, even when my mood was fine.

Do the experiences you have, like hearing the woman's voice or seeing hidden warnings, ever occur completely independently of how you're feeling emotionally, like when you're not particularly down, excited, or stressed?

I... I thought I just said that. Um... yeah. Like I mentioned, there was that month where things were... quieter. I was sleeping okay, not feeling so... unstoppable. But I still heard the comments from behind the shelves. And I was still seeing those hidden warnings in my materials. It lasted for a few weeks, even when my mood was fine.
When you hear the woman's voice or see these hidden warnings, do they usually match how you're feeling at the time, like if you're worried or excited, or do they seem unrelated to your mood?
I... I don't really know. I haven't paid much attention to whether they match or not. Um... it doesn't really seem connected to anything. She just... says things. I'm not really sure.

Have you ever had these experiences—like hearing the woman’s voice or seeing hidden warnings—when you were not feeling down, excited, or stressed at all, like completely emotionally neutral at the time?

I... we keep talking about this. I thought I explained it already. Um... yes. There was that month where I was just... fine. Sleeping normally. Not feeling like I had to do everything all at once. Just... neutral, I guess. But she was still there. The voice behind the shelves. And the warnings in my studio materials. That went on for a few weeks, even though I wasn't feeling anything strong emotionally.

Can you recall if these experiences—like hearing the woman's voice or seeing warnings—have ever occurred when you were not feeling down, excited, or stressed at all, like when you were emotionally neutral?

I... we've gone over this. I... yes. I already said. There was that month where I was just... normal. I was sleeping okay. I wasn't feeling like I was on top of the world or anything. But the... the comments from behind the shelves didn't stop. And I was still seeing those things in my studio materials. It went on like that for a few weeks.
Can you tell me more about the hidden warnings you see in your studio materials? Are they things that could have a realistic explanation, or do they seem completely strange or impossible to others?

I... I guess other people think it's strange. Um... like, I'll see certain stains on my materials, or... the way a seam is sewn... and I just know it's a warning. Or an instruction about my work. It happens with phrases in gallery emails, too. I just know they're meant specifically for me. 

Sometimes people try to show me a... a more ordinary explanation for it. They say it's just a regular email or a normal stain. But... it's very hard for me to let it go, even when they do that. I don't really want to explain it to them anymore.
Can you think of a time when you experienced the voice or the warnings when you were not feeling emotionally high, low, or stressed at all—like completely emotionally neutral?

I... we just talked about this. I'm not sure why we keep going over it. But, yes. Like I said... there was that quieter month. I was sleeping more normally. I didn't have that feeling of being unstoppable. But... the comments from behind the shelves were still there. And I was still seeing the warnings in my studio materials. It lasted for several weeks like that.
Can you think of a specific time when you were completely emotionally neutral—like neither happy, sad, nor stressed—and still experienced the voice or the warnings?

I... I really don't understand why we keep looping back to this. I just told you. Yes. 

There was a quieter month. I was sleeping normally, and I didn't feel unstoppable or anything... but I still kept hearing those comments from behind the shelves. And I was still reading those hidden warnings into my ordinary studio materials. It went on for several weeks like that. 

I don't... I don't have anything else to add about it.

Can you tell me more about how you know the stains or seams in your materials are warnings or instructions? Do they seem to follow a logic that others might understand, or do they feel completely unique and strange, like something that no one else would naturally see or believe?

I... I don't know how to explain it so you'll understand. It just... it feels unique to me, I guess. Like no one else would see it. 

I just... I look at a stain on a canvas, or the way a seam is folded, or a phrase in an email from a gallery... and I just know it's meant for me. It's an instruction. Or a warning. People try to tell me it's just a coffee stain or a typo, but... I can't just let it go. Even when they try to show me it's normal. I just know what it is.

Even when others give you clear explanations for things—like a stain being just a stain or a phrase being just a regular sentence—do you still believe strongly that they are actually warnings or instructions meant for you, no matter how much others try to explain otherwise?

Yeah. I do. 

Like I said... they try to explain it away. They say it's just coffee, or a typo in an email from the gallery. But... it doesn't change anything for me. I just... I still know it's a warning. Or an instruction. It's really hard to just let it go, even when they tell me it's nothing. I just can't.
